newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin returns to Moscow after long vacation.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin returns to Moscow after long vacation.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin returned to Moscow on Tuesday from a month-long vacation in which he kept up a busy workload, Itar-Tass news agency said.

Yeltsin went on holiday in early July, dividing his time between northwestern Karelia and the central Samara region where he fished in waters said by Russian media to have been specially stocked for him.
Apart from fishing, hunting, tennis and regular trips to the sauna, Yeltsin received many senior officials, signed documents and gave radio addresses to the nation.
On Monday he announced that the rouble would be redenominated from January 1, 1998 in a move that underlined Russia's growing economic confidence as inflation tumbles and market reforms take root.
Yeltsin, 66, has staged a strong recovery from last winter's quintuple heart bypass surgery and faces a hectic schedule in the coming months, including visits to France, China and Sweden.

He has also ordered officials to start preparing an informal meeting with Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto and is due to host the presidents of Germany, Egypt, France and the Philippines, and Italy's prime minister in Moscow.
